articles.title: In 2002, an 80-acre California town became the first town ever offered on eBay and drew 250 bids; 24 years later, Bridgeville is going up for sale again
articles.summary: News News: Bridgeville, a small town in Northern California, made history in 2002 when it was put up for sale on eBay. The 80-acre property attracted 250 bids du.
articles.body: Bridgeville, a small town in Northern California, made history in 2002 when it was put up for sale on eBay. The 80-acre property attracted 250 bids during a month-long auction, with the highest bid reaching $1,777,877. Now, 24 years later, Bridgeville is preparing to return to the property market.Located along the Van Duzen River, Bridgeville is about 45 miles southeast of Eureka and 26 miles east of Fortuna, according to Realtor.com. The rural community has an estimated population of only 25 people and is surrounded by redwood trees. The property has gone through several owners since it first gained attention on eBay.The town was initially listed by its former owner, Elizabeth Lapple, with a minimum bid of $775,000. Although the auction attracted strong interest, the winning bidder later backed out after learning about the amount of work the town needed. According to the report, several other potential deals also failed.Two years later, in 2004, financial adviser Bruce Krall from Orange County, California, bought Bridgeville for $700,000. The deal included 10 houses, four cabins, a post office, a cemetery and several other structures. Krall reportedly wanted to turn the town into a health spa, but later realised he could not afford the restoration work and put it back on eBay in 2006.New owner had different visionIn 2006, Bridgeville was bought for $1.25 million by Daniel LaPaille, a 25-year-old entertainment manager from Los Angeles. LaPaille wanted to give the small town a new direction by developing it as a self-sufficient, off-grid destination.However, LaPaille died by suicide months after purchasing the property. His family later became the owners of Bridgeville and has continued to look for someone who could take forward at least part of the vision he had for the town.“It was all about community for him,” Cindy LaPaille, Daniel’s mother and the current owner of Bridgeville, told Realtor.She said she hopes the next owner will be interested in building up the local community. “I would like to see somebody who is really wanting to see the community flourish,” she said.Cindy added that an ideal buyer would be able to live in Bridgeville, something she cannot do because she lives in Southern California. The family has received various suggestions over the years about how the property could be developed.Small community surrounded by natureDespite its small population, Bridgeville continues to have an active community. Residents use the town’s school as a meeting space. This allows them to stay involved, although the limited space also restricts the types of meetings that can be held.“There are a lot of great people out here. They all love community, they all love nature. They probably wouldn’t live out here if they didn’t,” Cindy said.The town also has several fruit trees, including pear, plum and apple trees. Blackberry bushes can also be found across the property. Wildlife is another part of everyday life in Bridgeville.“We have two resident bears, lots of deer, wild turkey ... if you’re sitting out here, you can always just look across and see something. ... We have it all,” Cindy said. “I’m told we have a bobcat. But that I haven’t seen.”The family has also been encouraged to turn Bridgeville into an Airbnb destination to attract people interested in nature. Cindy said the family had considered different options but had also tried to keep LaPaille’s original dream alive.“We kind of held out a few times trying to fulfill his dream. It’s an interesting process here,” she said.Going back on the marketBridgeville has been on and off the market since 2014. Its asking price has never again crossed the nearly $1.8 million mark reached by the winning eBay bid in 2002. The property was listed for as much as $1.5 million in 2023 and was most recently listed for $1.2 million in March 2025.The town is expected to be listed again later in September by Derek Baca of Madrone Realty. The exact asking price has not yet been confirmed, and it is also unclear which structures will be included in the new listing.Baca said potential buyers have already asked about what could be developed on the property. Suggestions have included adding cabins and creating an RV park. “Yes, you can absolutely do all those things,” Baca said.He explained that Humboldt County is open to economic development. Even if a proposed project does not fit the existing zoning, buyers can go through the planning and building process to have the property rezoned or reclassified, he said. Bridgeville also has public power, despite LaPaille's original plan for an off-grid community.Baca believes the town could have potential for development if a buyer is willing to invest in it. “It is a place that if somebody had the money to develop and turn into something, I think it would flourish 12 months out of the year,” he said.He also highlighted Bridgeville’s location between Highway 5 and Highway 101. According to Baca, this makes it “a good middle ground” for people travelling through the area.He suggested that facilities such as a gas station, a food truck or even a solar-powered electric vehicle charging station could serve travellers passing through.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 'Not intended to hurt anyone': CM Vijay clarifies gesture in TN assembly after DMK protest
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday clarified that a gesture he made during his As.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday clarified that a gesture he made during his Assembly speech was inadvertent and "not in any way intentional" . This comes as DMK accused him of attempting to body-shame former chief minister MK Stalin.The clarification came amid a major uproar in the Tamil Nadu assembly, where DMK MLAs demanded that Vijay's remarks, including references based on Enforcement Directorate documents and the Sarkaria Commission, be expunged from the records. The protesting legislators were later evicted from the House by marshals after Speaker JCD Prabhakar rejected their demand.In a post on X, Vijay said his body language during his response to the police department's grant request on September 7 should not be interpreted as a personal attack."I wish to clarify that, during my response speech on the police department's grant request in the Legislative Assembly on 7.9.2026, my body language, which inadvertently came across in between, was not in any way intentional. Therefore, I kindly request that it not be interpreted as an act intended to hurt anyone's feelings on a personal level," Vijay said.The controversy centres on a gesture Vijay made while referring to the history of the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), when he placed his right palm against his jaw. The gesture was widely interpreted as a reference to Stalin's broken jaw, which he suffered after being assaulted during his detention under MISA during the Emergency.CPI(M) leader P Shanmugam criticised Vijay, accusing him of making a personal attack on Stalin."It is a well-known historical fact that the Emergency period in India witnessed massive struggles to protect democracy, accompanied by repression and excesses. During that time, former chief minister MK Stalin was brutally assaulted by the police, resulting in a broken jaw," Shanmugam said in a post on X."Ridiculing someone's physical appearance is condemnable, regardless of who engages in it; for the Chief Minister himself to do so is an act of irresponsibility," he added.DMK protests over Vijay's remarksThe assembly witnessed heated exchanges on Tuesday after DMK Whip EV Velu demanded that Vijay's references to ED allegations of graft and the Sarkaria Commission be removed from the records.Velu also objected to references to people who were not present in the House to defend themselves, as well as references to deceased individuals.He argued that the Sarkaria Commission had examined 28 charges and claimed that no legal action could follow as the charges were not proved."Bringing this up without evidence is misleading," he contended.Velu also objected to Vijay's references to the MISA period, saying that repeated discussion of the issue and personal attacks on individuals were inappropriate.State law minister R Nirmal Kumar defended Vijay's remarks, saying they were based on official ED documents and the Sarkaria Commission report. He also reiterated allegations of corruption against the then DMK regime.Kumar disputed claims concerning Stalin's arrest under MISA, arguing that it was linked to derogatory comments made against former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi regarding her "21-point programme".Leader of the House K A Sengottaiyan said there was no reason to expunge Vijay's remarks, citing a precedent in which late Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa had also spoken about the issue.The DMK members continued to protest after Speaker Prabhakar ruled against expunging the remarks. Several MLAs gathered before the Speaker's podium and raised slogans despite repeated appeals to return to their seats.Prabhakar eventually ordered marshals to evict the protesting MLAs. The legislators continued raising slogans as they were taken out of the Assembly hall.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: No rooms, Rs 2.3 lakh a night: BRICS Summit sends Delhi hotel rates soaring
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: As India prepares to host the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, luxury hotels in the national capital are facing a sharp squeeze in room availabi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As India prepares to host the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, luxury hotels in the national capital are facing a sharp squeeze in room availability, with tariffs at some marquee properties climbing beyond Rs 2 lakh a night ahead of the September 12-13 gathering.The summit, which brings leaders of the expanded BRICS grouping to Delhi and marks two decades since the bloc’s founding, is driving concentrated demand for high-end accommodation, with several premium hotels showing limited or no availability and others quoting rates of more than Rs 2 lakh per night, according to news agency PTI.Booking checks showed no room availability at Taj Mahal and The Oberoi in New Delhi for September 11-12, while Taj Palace had no rooms available for September 10-12. The Leela Palace, New Delhi, was also not accepting bookings for stays between September 10 and 12.At ITC Maurya, New Delhi, rooms available for September 10-13 were commanding tariffs starting at more than Rs 2.3 lakh a night.The surge comes as delegates and other visitors are expected to arrive in the capital ahead of the two-day summit and extend their stays, putting pressure on room inventory, particularly in central Delhi.K B Kachru, president, Hotel Association of India (HAI) and Chairman - South Asia, Radisson Hotel Group, said the summit was highlighting the pressure on India's hospitality infrastructure."India is commanding global attention at a defining moment -- as the nation prepares to host marquee international events and cements its position as a premier MICE destination, the world is watching how we scale to meet our tourism targets."The BRICS Summit alone will put considerable focus on room inventory and that spotlight is exposing a hard truth: our hospitality infrastructure has not kept pace with our tourism ambition," he said, according to PTI.Kachru said India currently has only about 200,000-220,000 branded hotel rooms, which he described as inadequate for the country's tourism ambitions.The demand is also being felt beyond central Delhi. Rahool Macarius, Market Managing Director, Eurasia, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, said the summit was creating a distinct demand pattern across Delhi-NCR."At Ramada Encore by Wyndham, Dwarka Expressway, this event-led demand is reflected in occupancy for September 12-15, currently tracking at 65 per cent, significantly ahead of the broader market demand," he said.For tourists, business travellers and families visiting Delhi during the period, the squeeze could mean higher accommodation costs or a shift towards hotels outside central areas and lower-priced properties.However, hotel tariffs and availability remain dynamic and can change with bookings, cancellations and fresh inventory releases. articles.title: Ukraine unveils ‘Koral’: New missile built to take on ballistic threats
articles.summary: International News: Ukraine has for the first time shown the launcher for its homegrown Koral surface-to-air missile, a new air-defence weapon being developed to tackle b.
articles.body: Ukraine has for the first time shown the launcher for its homegrown Koral surface-to-air missile, a new air-defence weapon being developed to tackle both aircraft and ballistic targets. The system was displayed at the MSPO defence exhibition in Poland on September 8, according to Ukrainian defence outlet Militarnyi.An image released by Ukraine’s state defence industry showed a Koral missile being launched from a self-propelled platform mounted on a Czech-made Tatra truck. The missile is primarily designed to intercept aerial threats, including ballistic targets. Its developers say it could also be used in limited circumstances against radar-detectable targets on land or at sea.The latest version of Koral weighs around 450 kg and carries a 36-kg warhead. It is 4.8 metres long, with a body diameter of 230/300 mm. Its guidance system combines inertial navigation, radio-command updates and an active radar seeker. This allows the missile to receive corrections during flight before using its own radar to guide itself towards the target in the final stage.The weapon is the result of a project that has changed considerably since it was first presented. Development began in 2016, when Koral was proposed as part of a ship-based air-defence system.The latest design is longer and roughly 50% heavier than that early version, while its warhead has increased from 25 kg to 36 kg. Ukraine has not publicly disclosed the current missile’s maximum range, according to a United24 Media report.Koral was initially planned as part of a wider family of Ukrainian air-defence systems covering different ranges. Its developers had also explored versions for land and naval use, as well as a possible air-to-air variant.The unveiling comes as Ukraine continues efforts to strengthen its domestic air-defence capabilities amid the ongoing war with Russia. The new Koral configuration shows how the project has evolved from an earlier medium-range concept into a system intended to address a wider range of aerial threats.

articles.title: UK-Israel spat gets ugly: Tel Aviv to close British consulate in Jerusalem over sanctions on settlers
articles.summary: Middle East News: Israel on Tuesday announced plans to close Britain’s consulate in East Jerusalem and take further measures against the UK. The move comes in retaliati.
articles.body: Israel on Tuesday announced plans to close Britain’s consulate in East Jerusalem and take further measures against the UK. The move comes in retaliation for London’s sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said.According to news agency Reuters, Saar said the consulate, which is accredited to the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank, would be shut following Britain’s decision to ban imports from Israeli settlements.He also announced that Britain would no longer be allowed to participate in the US-led coordination mission for Gaza and that British training of Palestinian Authority forces in the West Bank would be terminated, according to the Israeli foreign minister.Saar further said that Israel will prevent the entry into Israel of 12 elected UK officials, as well as other British citizens Sa’ar said were “involved in antisemitic and anti-Israel activity.”The announcement came after Britain, France, Canada and 12 other countries moved to restrict imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, where it says “settler terrorists” are carrying out “ethnic cleansing” of Palestinians. Britain also said it would target companies and individuals involved in financing, construction, infrastructure and other activities linked to settlement expansion.British foreign secretary Ed Miliband told the House of Commons, “So I can announce today that we will introduce an import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories.”He added, “So to those who finance or facilitate illegal settlements, let me say this, you will face the full force of UK sanctions. Settlements are illegal. They should not be promoted in our country.”Miliband also said Britain could no longer simply “call out” injustice and suffering, while describing the situation in parts of the West Bank as ethnic cleansing.The economic impact of the ban is expected to be limited, as Israeli settlements produce few exports, mainly agricultural. However, the move signals growing discontent among Israel’s allies. Miliband said he felt “a deep sense of shame” over Palestine. Settlement expansion has accelerated under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government.Israel’s response followed calls from finance minister Bezalel Smotrich for the immediate expulsion of the British ambassador. Smotrich said Israel would not be a “doormat” to what he described as the “antisemitic” government of the UK.President Isaac Herzog separately accused Britain of interfering in Israel’s upcoming elections, which are due in late October.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Glowworms return to a North Yorkshire reserve after more than 100 years; larvae raised in a Bristol garden shed have produced the first glowing females
articles.summary: UK News: Glowworms have returned to a North Yorkshire nature reserve after more than 100 years, following a conservation project that began with larvae being r.
articles.body: Glowworms have returned to a North Yorkshire nature reserve after more than 100 years, following a conservation project that began with larvae being raised in a Bristol garden shed. The first glowing females have now been recorded at Nosterfield nature reserve, providing an early sign that the reintroduction of the endangered beetles is progressing. Volunteers from the Lower Ure Conservation Trust counted up to 12 glowing females over several weeks this summer, two years after hundreds of captive-reared larvae were released at the site. Independent ecologist Pete Cooper, who led the breeding work, told The Guardian, “It’s a really great first indicator of initial success.” The project began with a small number of glowworms collected from an authorised local donor site. Cooper bred them in captivity and reared their larvae in Bristol. Further releases are planned, with 1,900 more larvae due to be introduced at Nosterfield later this year.First glowing females show the glowworms are backVolunteers from the Lower Ure Conservation Trust counted as many as 12 glowing females over successive weeks this summer. The observations provided an early indication that the released larvae had survived and completed their development at the reserve. Female glowworms are flightless and use their bioluminescent glow to attract males, which have weaker flight capabilities and do not produce the same visible light.For Cooper, who has worked on breeding and releasing glowworms for six years without being part of the project, the sightings represented an important stage in the reintroduction. Cooper added that the sightings showed that “glowworms can live out their full life cycle at this site”, citing the availability of food and for mating as signs that the reserve can support the species.Nosterfield was once home to many glowwormsHistorical records show that glowworms were once present in Nosterfield in large numbers. In 1909, writer Edmund Bogg described the insects as being “wont to hang out their fieldstar lamps … as if lit by the hands of fairy folk”. Their disappearance from Nosterfield followed quarrying, while glowworms have also declined elsewhere across Britain.The source identifies several factors behind the wider decline, including more intensive farming, development and electric lighting. The loss of rough and varied grassland has also affected the habitats the beetles need. At Nosterfield, the Lower Ure Conservation Trust began restoring former quarry land after purchasing its first 72 acres of disused quarry in 1997. The area has gradually been converted into species-rich wetland and grassland on magnesian limestone, with the charity eventually expected to manage almost 600 acres for wildlife.Project will release 1,900 more glowworm larvaeThe project is continuing beyond the first sightings. With assistance from volunteers at Westbury Wildlife Park Foundation, Cooper has bred another 1,900 glowworm larvae, which are due to be released at Nosterfield later this year. The Lower Ure Conservation Trust has also worked with volunteers to adjust habitat management and monitor the glowworms as they emerge.The reserve's director, Simon Warwick, credited Cooper and the volunteers involved in the project. He said the return of the species reflected “the raw passion and enthusiasm” of Cooper and the contribution of the 80 volunteers working at the nature reserve. Warwick also said the glowworms were “incredibly rare in the region” and that volunteers were excited by their return. Cooper said the reserve's population would not be confirmed as self-sustaining until 2030, when offspring from this year's wild adults are expected to reach maturity.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Mother of twin girls given less than 10% chance of survival after TTTS at 16 weeks; after surgery, premature birth and 300 days in hospital, twins now prepare for first day of school
articles.summary: UK News: A mother whose twin daughters were given less than a 10 per cent chance of survival after a devastating pregnancy complication is celebrating a milest.
articles.body: A mother whose twin daughters were given less than a 10 per cent chance of survival after a devastating pregnancy complication is celebrating a milestone she once feared she would never witness: Ruby and Scarlett are starting school.Hanna Brameld, 44, from Beckenham, was just 16 weeks pregnant when doctors discovered that her unborn daughters had Twin-to-Twin Transfusion Syndrome (TTTS), a potentially life-threatening complication that can occur in twin pregnancies sharing a placenta.The condition was detected during a routine scan after a sonographer noticed that blood was not being distributed evenly between the babies. In TTTS, abnormal blood-vessel connections in the shared placenta can cause one twin to receive too much blood while the other receives too little, putting both babies at serious risk.‘I felt like the floor had disappeared beneath me’Brameld said she was left “frozen” when doctors explained the severity of the condition. A consultant told her and her husband, James, that without a risky operation, the chances of both babies surviving were less than 10 per cent.“I felt like the floor had disappeared beneath me,” she told the Daily Mail. “These were my babies. I hadn't even met them yet, and already I was being asked to imagine losing them.”Just a week later, Brameld underwent a complex procedure in which a specialist surgeon operated inside her womb to treat the condition.Thankfully, the operation was successful. But the family was soon confronted with another frightening complication: the procedure ruptured Brameld’s waters, causing the protective fluid surrounding the twins to fall to dangerously low levels.Doctors warned that Scarlett’s lungs might not develop properly.“I was terrified,” Brameld recalled.Pregnancy became a day-by-day battleThe couple began attending King's College Hospital every week for scans to monitor the twins.Determined to give her daughters every possible chance, Brameld said she did everything she could to prolong the pregnancy.“I drank glass after glass of blackcurrant squash, convinced it might somehow help,” she said. “I stayed as still as possible, willing my body to hold on just a little longer.”For the mother, every additional day without labour represented hope.“Every single day that passed without going into labour felt like a small victory,” she said.Eventually, Ruby and Scarlett were delivered by emergency Caesarean section in 2021.Ruby weighed just 1lb 10.5oz, while Scarlett weighed 2lb 3oz. Both babies were immediately placed on ventilators, and their mother had to wait 10 agonising days before she could hold them.The twins spent 300 days in hospitalTheir premature birth marked the beginning of another difficult chapter for the Brameld family, with both babies facing serious medical complications during their prolonged stays in neonatal care.Ruby battled a suspected severe bowel infection and meningitis.Scarlett suffered a collapsed lung, required treatment to close a hole in her heart and developed sepsis caused by the bacteria Serratia marcescens.“I have never felt so helpless,” Brameld said, describing the emotional strain of caring for two critically ill newborns.“I was desperate to be beside Scarlett every second, but Ruby needed me too - feeding every three hours, needing to be changed, needing her mum.”She also had to express breast milk, eat, sleep and cope emotionally while moving between hospital rooms.Ruby went home, but Scarlett needed prolonged careRuby was finally discharged three months after her birth, coinciding with the twins’ original due date.But Scarlett remained in hospital and continued to require significant medical support. She needed long-term respiratory assistance, including a ventilator overnight, as well as a surgically fitted feeding tube.Ruby’s mother continued taking her back to hospital every day so she could remain close to her sister.The family spent weeks learning how to manage Scarlett’s complex care before she was eventually discharged.Between them, Ruby and Scarlett spent a total of 300 days in hospital.“I will never forget carrying Scarlett through our front door and watching her and Ruby together as a family, at last,” Brameld said.From neonatal intensive care to the school gatesNow, years after their parents were warned that they might not survive the pregnancy, Ruby and Scarlett are preparing to start school.Their mother describes them today as “double trouble” - energetic, inseparable and full of life.The twins have also taken on a fundraising challenge of their own, completing their first sponsored run: a one-mile event in Greenwich in support of neonatal charity Ickle Pickles, which supported the family during their time in neonatal intensive care.The experience had such a profound impact on Brameld that she left her career in the fashion industry to work for the charity. She now provides peer-to-peer support to parents facing situations similar to the one her family experienced and returns to King's College Hospital every fortnight.Ickle Pickles supports families of premature and sick newborns and helps hospitals obtain vital neonatal equipment.‘It takes my breath away’Looking back at everything her daughters have endured, Brameld said seeing them run together is almost impossible to comprehend.“When I think about everything my girls have overcome - a less than 10 per cent chance of survival, a desperate operation, months apart in separate hospital rooms - and then I watch them running down the street together, laughing, holding hands on their way into school, it takes my breath away,” she said.“Ruby and Scarlett are living proof that even when the odds feel impossible, miracles can still happen.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to engage "frankly and constructively" with China, discussing domestic security, Hong Kong, and human rights cases in his first phone call with President Xi Jinping.

Burnham and Xi Jinping affirm commitment to a long-term comprehensive strategic partnership between the UK and China, emphasizing pragmatic cooperation in advancing shared global challenges and economic growth.

Both leaders agree to continue dialogue on mutual priorities, with Burnham expressing condolences for lives lost in recent floods on the Nepal-China border and appreciation for rescue efforts supporting affected British nationals.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham vowed to engage "frankly and constructively" with China while raising domestic security, Hong Kong and human rights cases in his first phone call with President Xi Jinping.

The prime minister discussed the "importance of pragmatic cooperation" with the Chinese leader as they spoke on Tuesday morning, Downing Street said.

In a readout of the talks, a No 10 spokesperson said: "The Prime Minister expressed his sincere condolences for the lives lost in recent floods on the Nepal-China border and his appreciation for the rescue efforts and support for British nationals affected."

"Both leaders affirmed their commitment to a long-term and consistent comprehensive strategic partnership between the UK and China," the spokesperson added.

"As Permanent Members of the Security Council and major economies, they discussed the importance of pragmatic cooperation in advancing UK and Chinese interests and addressing shared global challenges."

"They discussed the opportunities in the UK-China relationship including on economic growth and improving living standards for people in both their countries."

"The Prime Minister said that he would engage frankly and constructively on issues that matter for both countries, and raised domestic security, Russia's war in Ukraine, Hong Kong, human rights and consular cases of particular importance."

"The leaders agreed to stay in touch, and that dialogue between their governments on a range of mutual priorities would continue." #

articles.title: Nearly 300 flights cancelled across UK after air traffic control glitch, major airports hit
articles.summary: Europe News: Nearly 300 flights were cancelled across the UK on Tuesday after a technical problem in the air traffic control system disrupted operations at several.
articles.body: Nearly 300 flights were cancelled across the UK on Tuesday after a technical problem in the air traffic control system disrupted operations at several major airports, with hundreds more flights delayed.Britain’s National Air Traffic Services (NATS) said engineers had identified the problem in its flight processing system and were working urgently to restore normal operations.“We have identified that the issue was in our flight processing system. Our engineers are on site and working urgently to resume normal operations as quickly as possible,” NATS said in a statement.The air traffic control provider later said it had implemented a fix and that its flight system was beginning to recover.“Flights are still departing and airspace is open, but recovery will take some time,” NATS said earlier.According to news agency AP, citing flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the technical issue disrupted departing flights across the London flight information region, with arrivals and departures being regulated as a result.Heathrow, Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted were among the airports affected. Heathrow said it was working with NATS to resolve the problem and advised passengers to check their flight status with their airline.According to FlightAware data, about 100 flights had been cancelled at Heathrow, while 367 were delayed. At Gatwick, about 250 flights were delayed, accounting for roughly 31 per cent of the airport’s total flights, the data showed.Acccording to Reuters, other airports reporting disruptions included Luton, Birmingham, Aberdeen, Glasgow and Edinburgh. Edinburgh Airport said the issue might affect its operations, while Dublin Airport warned that some flights arriving from and departing for the UK would face delays.British Airways said it was experiencing disruption because of the air traffic control problem.“This is entirely out of our control and we're in touch with our customers whilst our teams work to get them on their way as quickly as possible,” the airline said.EasyJet said the issue was causing delays across Europe. Ryanair, Wizz Air and Virgin Atlantic were not immediately available for comment.The disruption comes after previous NATS incidents. In 2024, Britain’s aviation regulator said NATS needed to review its contingency plans after an automatic flight-plan processing failure the previous year caused widespread disruption. Airline bosses estimated the incident cost more than £100 million in refunds and compensation.A separate radar-related technical issue in July last year disrupted flights for more than four hours at major airports, including Heathrow.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia, India plan BrahMos upgrade ahead of PM Modi-Putin meeting
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: Russia and India are exploring an upgrade of the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile to add new capabilities, improve its effectiveness and m.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Russia and India are exploring an upgrade of the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile to add new capabilities, improve its effectiveness and make it more competitive in international markets, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday.“We are jointly producing the BrahMos missiles, and it is time to think about improving those missiles, adding some additional characteristics, making them more competitive in the market and more effective,” Peskov said during a virtual briefing with Indian journalists.His comments came ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to India, with Peskov confirming that Putin and Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet in New Delhi on Friday on the sidelines of the BRICS summit.The meeting will be their second bilateral engagement in a month and is expected to cover defence, energy, technology, trade and investment ties.BrahMos upgrade, S-400 and Su-57 on agendaPeskov said Russia remains committed to completing deliveries of the S-400 air defence systems to India and is also discussing the possible supply of its Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jets.He said Moscow is willing to share technology with India, including technology related to the Su-57, as the two countries seek to deepen defence cooperation beyond a traditional buyer-seller relationship.Russia remains one of India's major defence suppliers, although New Delhi has increasingly diversified its procurement towards countries including the US, France and Israel.Russia accounted for about 40% of India's major arms imports between 2021 and 2025, down from 51% in the previous five-year period, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.India operates hundreds of Russian-made fighter aircraft and several S-400 systems. The air defence system was used during the four-day India-Pakistan conflict in May 2025.India is also in the process of procuring a new batch of fifth-generation fighter aircraft. The Rafale, F-21, F/A-18 and Eurofighter Typhoon are among the aircraft being considered, while Russia is pitching the Su-57.Russia backs India's Ukraine peace effortsPeskov said Moscow would welcome India's efforts to contribute to ending the war in Ukraine, saying Russia's position broadly aligns with New Delhi's call for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.“We know the position of India on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent, it corresponds with our own position because we do want the solution to the Ukraine conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open for this process,” Peskov said.He added that Putin understands India's position on the conflict and is expected to brief Modi on the situation during their meeting.“We welcome the willingness of the Indian side to contribute. We also welcome the efforts of American President (Donald) Trump,” Peskov said.Modi had met Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek last week, where he called for an immediate end to the conflict and urged the Russian leader to move from "endless war towards end of war."External affairs minister S Jaishankar later travelled to Kyiv and said India was ready to contribute whatever it could to efforts to bring peace to Ukraine.

articles.title: Coast Guard joins search for missing plane near Bahamas
articles.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard joined the search for a missing plane carrying four family members that vanished near the Bahamas on their way back to Florida. “The Royal Bahamian Defense Force requested Coast Guard assistance following a report of a downed airplane with 4 people aboard approximately 15 miles off Andros Island, Bahamas,” a spokesperson…
articles.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard joined the search for a missing plane carrying four family members that vanished near the Bahamas on their way back to Florida.

“The Royal Bahamian Defense Force requested Coast Guard assistance following a report of a downed airplane with 4 people aboard approximately 15 miles off Andros Island, Bahamas,” a spokesperson for the Coast Guard told The Hill.

The passengers have been identified as pilot Mario Lamar, 80; his wife Lili Lamar, 79; and two of their grandchildren, Sofia Sosa, 28; and Christian Sosa, 22.

An NBC affiliate station reported that all four family members were found deceased.

“The search and recovery mission was conducted alongside family members and civilians who answered our call for help,” a statement from the family read.

The investigation is still ongoing, according to the Coast Guard. Bahamian and U.S. forces had to temporarily pause rescue efforts in the morning amid bad weather.

Bahamian authorities believe the plane initially crash-landed off the coast of Red Bays, North Andros — approximately 160 miles from Miami, Florida.

“Police on the island of Andros are coordinating efforts to locate an aircraft,” the agency said, according to The Associated Press .

articles.title: US issues sweeping sanctions against Iranian airlines, foreign businesses
articles.summary: The Trump administration on Tuesday announced new sanctions against all of Iran’s airlines and nearly a dozen foreign companies doing business with Iran’s Mahan Air, which had earlier been sanctioned for its ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The sanctions are part of Operation Economic Outcast, a financial pressure campaign that the administration…
articles.body:
The Trump administration on Tuesday announced new sanctions against all of Iran’s airlines and nearly a dozen foreign companies doing business with Iran’s Mahan Air, which had earlier been sanctioned for its ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The sanctions are part of Operation Economic Outcast, a financial pressure campaign that the administration launched last month as the military front of the more than six-month war stalled out.

The newest sanctions target 27 Iranian airlines and nine entities, cargo service providers and general sales agents that the Treasury Department said the IRGC has used to obtain American aircraft or other U.S.-origin aviation materials.

This includes sanctioning several firms based in Turkey and the United Arab Emirates for helping Mahan Air secure at least three Boeing B-777 aircraft this summer. The aircraft originated from a retired fleet and passed through ECT Aviation Support UAE, where they received temporary registrations, the Treasury Department said.

Mahan Air was originally sanctioned in 2011 for being a critical asset for the IRGC, the military branch tasked with ensuring the survival of the Islamic Republic, responsible for global terrorist attacks and a sponsor of proxy military groups across the Middle East.

“Under Operation Economic Outcast, we promised severe consequences for those providing financial lifelines to the Iranian regime,” Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent said in a statement.

“Today, we followed through on that promise with sanctions on companies that continue to support Mahan Air. Let this be a warning to anyone doing business with Iran’s remaining airlines, all of which we sanctioned today: You are at risk of being cut off from the global financial system.”

Other sanctions targeted Ali Mohamed Mohamed Mahran, a UAE-based Egyptian national who serves as the chief executive of ECT Aviation Support UAE, and the British unit of the firm.

The Treasury Department also sanctioned Turkey-based firms that have coordinated shipments, including drone components and industrial equipment destined for Iran, on behalf of Mahan Air, and it sanctioned a Turkey-based entity that has served as a general sales agent for Mahan Air and coordinated shipments on behalf of the blacklisted airline.

Other sanctioned entities with ties to Mahan are based in Malaysia and Kazakhstan.

As a result of the sanctions, all property and interests in the U.S. of the sanctioned entities are blocked, and Americans are generally blocked from doing business with the blacklisted entities.

Bessent has promoted the administration’s economic pressure campaign against Iran as an “economic D-day” that has the goal of financially asphyxiating the Iranian regime.

One of the first major actions targeted a UAE-based branch of an Egyptian bank , and the U.S. later announced sanctions against the Turkey-based Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries. The Treasury Department said Golden Global Bank facilitated tens of millions of dollars’ worth of transactions for the IRGC.

articles.title: US Democrat urges House Speaker to sue Trump admin over triumphal arch, says Congress never approved funds
articles.summary: US News: House Democrat Chellie Pingree demands Speaker Mike Johnson take legal action against the Trump administration for starting work on a triumphal arch in Washington without Congressional approval. This move raises questions about funding and authority for the project.
articles.body: A senior House Democrat has urged Speaker Mike Johnson to sue the Trump administration over plans to begin work on a proposed triumphal arch in Washington, arguing that Congress has not approved funding or authorised the project.Representative Chellie Pingree, the top Democrat on the House subcommittee overseeing funding for national parks, made the request in a letter to Johnson on Tuesday, Reuters reported."Congress has neither appropriated funding nor granted authority for this project," Pingree wrote. She accused the administration of moving ahead on the project despite the lack of congressional approval and asked Johnson to "file suit immediately" to prevent further work.Last week, US District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered the administration to give the court at least 48 hours' notice before carrying out work at the site. The order followed an announcement by the Interior Department that it intended to begin work despite the ongoing challenge and the monument not yet having received final approval from a federal planning body.The court order does allow archaeological work required under the National Historic Preservation Act. This includes digging to establish whether the site contains underground archaeological or cultural material.The government told the court it plans to excavate four test pits from September 21 or later. articles.title: Village head's appeal drove Ladakh LG's initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation
articles.summary: India News: SRINAGAR: Nearly 90 million litres of glacial water have started irrigating more than 1,000 acres of parched farmlands across 12 villages in Ladakh ev.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Nearly 90 million litres of glacial water have started irrigating more than 1,000 acres of parched farmlands across 12 villages in Ladakh every day, thanks to a pioneering initiative by lieutenant governor (LG) V K Saxena last month.The massive volume of glacier-melt, previously flowing untapped into the River Indus, is now being channelised from Stok village nallah in Leh into the Igoo-Phey Irrigation Canal using simple earthwork that incurred little capital expenditure.It was an appeal from a village chief that drove the LG to brainstorm on harnessing glaciers and snowmelt for productive use. According to officials, Saxena was on a visit to Chuchot village in Leh where the ‘goba’ (or nambardar, the traditional village head), Mirza Hussain, sought his intervention to address the acute water shortage in the village.The plea prompted the LG to spearhead a comprehensive and systematic campaign to identify locations where large volumes of glacial water were flowing down unused, draining straight into the Indus, even as surrounding farmlands remained dry, officials said.The govt first identified Stok village nallah, fed by the Stok Kangri Glacier, as one such place where glacier water could be diverted into the existing canal. Officials said the discharge from Stok nallah was assessed at 36 cusecs, or approximately 90 million litres of water in 24 hours.Two channels were then created to divert nearly 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal — 62 million litres toward Igoo village upstream and approximately 18 million litres toward Phey village downstream.This daily flow has substantially augmented the total water flow in the Igoo-Phey Canal — from 50 cusecs to nearly 90 cusecs. As a result, water supply will be guaranteed daily to the 12 villages fed by the canal. Previously, water from the 43-km-long Igoo-Phey Canal was distributed to villages on a restrictive roster basis due to limited availability.Having successfully channelised 80 million litres of water into the Igoo-Phey Canal, the remaining 10 million litres were diverted into another dry canal at Chuchot, and will help irrigate farmland in and around the village, officials said.“The entire 90 million litres of water was tapped and the discharge from Stok Kangri glacier into the Indus River was reduced to zero in just two days at no cost,” said an official, adding that the success of the initiative serves as a blueprint for water management across the Union Territory.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Canada, France, UK to ban imports from Israeli settlements
articles.summary: Canada, France and the United Kingdom on Tuesday announced a joint ban on imported goods from Israeli settlements in what they called a “turning point” in the efforts to reach a two-state solution in the region. “One year ago, we recognized the State of Palestine,” the nations wrote in a statement. “The time has come…
articles.body:
Canada, France and the United Kingdom on Tuesday announced a joint ban on imported goods from Israeli settlements in what they called a “turning point” in the efforts to reach a two-state solution in the region.

“One year ago, we recognized the State of Palestine,” the nations wrote in a statement . “The time has come to take further action to uphold our commitment to protect the two-state solution, our interests and to stand up for our values, before it is too late.”

The statement from Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron follows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s decision to press forward with a controversial housing settlement in the E1 area of the West Bank.

The E1 section is a 4.5-square-mile area that lies to the east of Jerusalem. The Israeli government’s planned development on this land has long provoked fierce opposition from around the globe.

The Israeli government’s plan includes seven residential compounds with a total of 1,234 housing units, according to The Times of Israel . A tender published by Israel’s construction and housing ministry gives contractors until Oct. 19 to bid on this project.

“Systematic settlement expansion in the West Bank, including the Government of Israel’s latest decision to progress the E1 settlement, as well as the dramatic increase in settler violence, pose a direct and urgent threat to that vision for peace,” the heads of state wrote in their Tuesday letter.

At the same time, the leaders expressed their commitment to continuing to work with the Israeli government to ensure its sovereignty.

“In taking this coordinated action, we reiterate our desire for a close and productive partnership with Israel, our enduring support for the Israeli people and our unwavering commitment to Israel’s security,” they wrote. “We support a safe and secure Israel, living alongside a safe and secure Palestine.”

Several weeks ago, a group of Democratic U.S. senators also called on Netanyahu to reverse the planned E1 housing settlement.

“The United States must remain committed to a two-state solution that delivers lasting peace and security for both the Jewish, democratic State of Israel and for a future Palestinian state,” the Democrats wrote in their statement. “Construction in E1 would take us further away from that goal.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio responded to news of the joint ban on Tuesday, telling reporters the U.S. will “obviously” not participate in this action.

“We were made aware that they were going to make this decision,” Rubio told reporters . “We heard their argument as to why, but look, we share the goal of stability.”

“We don’t want to see some uptick in violence or an uptick in conflict or tensions in the West Bank at a very tenuous time in the region,” he added.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced in a Tuesday floor speech in the House of Commons that the U.K. government will take additional steps to block this settlement’s establishment, including sanctioning companies and individuals that support this construction and refusing arms licenses and other exports that could facilitate this expansion effort.

“Our argument is not with the people of Israel, with whom the U.K. has unshakable bonds,” Miliband said. “Our argument is with the conduct of its government.”

Israel’s foreign ministry responded to these new sanctions by announcing bans on 11 British lawmakers and a lawyer from entering Israel.

“The accusations made today by the foreign secretary in the British parliament were outrageous lies,” Gideon Sa’ar, the Israeli foreign minister, said in video remarks shared by his office on social media.

The list includes members of three of the U.K.’s political parties and attorney Fahad Ansari, who has represented Palestinian militant group Hamas’s political arm in British courts. Ansari said he took the ban as a “badge of honour” in a social media post .

Additionally, Israel announced it will close Britain’s consulate in East Jerusalem, remove British representatives from the International Gaza Support Center and that the U.K. will no longer participate in a U.S.-led mission to Gaza.

“The message to every government that harms us is clear: Whoever acts against Israel, Israel will act against them, and they will lose their influence and relevance in the region,” Sa’ar said. “Measures against Israel will not go unanswered.”

"Ensuring that we take care of our community and our residents and our people does mean making sure that we have emergency assistance available for what is probably one of the most challenging situations that you could possibly face," Board Vice Chair Maureen Coffey said. articles.title: Strategic autonomy in motion as India hosts Brics summit
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India will host the annual Brics summit on Sept 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India will host the annual Brics summit on Sept 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That gathering is remembered for the inclusion of the African Union in G20, marking a major step in efforts to bridge the gap between the western-led global order and the emerging Global South. At Brics, India will look to leverage that momentum, working with major emerging economies to demand structural reforms of global governance institutions dominated by the West.This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies - Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, the UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia - along with 10 other partner countries.The theme of India's 2026 chairship is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability', drawing inspiration from PM Narendra Modi's 'humanity first' and people-centric approach to Brics. Under its chairship, India has so far held over 350 meetings - 25 at the ministerial level, including the foreign ministers' and national security advisers' engagements.India for BricsDespite political fragmentation and economic imbalances, Brics remains important for India for multiple reasons, especially in an increasingly uncertain world. It reinforces India's strategic autonomy and multi-alignment policy, not allowing any one single bloc to acquire excessive leverage over it. That it can simultaneously expand its strategic and technology ties with the West and also work with Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific reaffirms an independent foreign policy.Brics also allows India to showcase its Global South leadership credentials, as it works with other major emerging markets to push for reforms of global institutions like UNSC, IMF and World Bank that are not representative of the developing world. Support for UNSC reforms is important, although it falls short of an explicit endorsement of India's permanent membership bid, mainly because of China's presence.India's approach to Brics is also guided by its complex ties with China. Turning away would mean allowing China to shape the agenda of the developing world. India's moderating influence prevents the bloc from turning into an anti-West platform.There's focus too on expanding financial architecture, as no govt would like its trade to be held hostage by instruments it cannot control. As foreign minister S Jaishankar has underlined, institutions such as New Development Bank and Contingent Reserve Arrangement demonstrate the group's ability to create credible alternatives. For India, these are not initiatives targeted at any currency.Brics also provides India with markets, along with trade diversification, de-risking and supply-chain opportunities. Brics' membership deepens India's trade ties with Russia (energy), Brazil (agriculture/commodities), Gulf and African countries, diversifying away from over-reliance on any single partner.Key challenges for IndiaThe first, of course, is to forge a consensus on West Asia that would enable a joint Brics declaration, a task complicated by the presence of the UAE and Iran in the group. India will likely focus on drafting a resolution rooted in the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection, while looking to ring-fence economic agreements from contentious political issues by acknowledging respective national positions.Balancing relations with the US is another key concern for India, which is hosting the summit fresh off a tariff firestorm with Washington. US President Donald Trump sees the grouping itself as an assault on US currency. India backs legitimate local-currency settlement while maintaining it is against any common Brics currency or China-centred replacement mechanism.Another challenge for India is to prevent China's predominance without destabilising its bilateral relations with Beijing. For all the talk about Brics' combined power, China enjoys a vastly asymmetrical influence with its trade, investment, manufacturing and critical mineral leverage. Wary of China's economic agenda, India avoided endorsing SCO's 2030 economic roadmap, and it must work with Beijing in Brics on shared objectives, though without letting the forum become a Chinese economic or geopolitical platform.This also intersects with the challenge of ensuring that an expanded grouping remains governable and cohesive, especially with countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh pursuing membership with support from Beijing.Jaishankar said while announcing the summit that Brics must transition now from a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery. In that spirit, India seems focused on delivering an outcome-oriented summit, with key deliverables like a unanimous Brics declaration, logistics supply-chain cooperation framework, incubator/startup network, development finance, cross-border payment and continued support for Indian priorities like UNSC reforms and counterterrorism.To conclude, inclusion of African Union was not the only major takeaway from 2023's G20 summit. Perhaps more dramatic was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine through a compromise language crafted by India, which allowed a G20 declaration. India can derive confidence from that diplomatic triumph as it heads into another tough but potentially rewarding global summit.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: In the low country of South Carolina, where blackwater rivers wind through cypress swamps and marshes give way to the Atlantic, a quiet but monumental act of conservation has just reshaped the landscape. Cox Enterprises, a major media and communications company, has donated development rights on nearly 4,400 acres of its Clarendon Farms property, locking in permanent protection for one of the most ecologically rich tracts in the Southeast. The land, valued at hundreds of millions of dollars, includes about 40 miles of river and marsh frontage that provide critical habitat for fish, waterfowl and countless other species. As announced by Ducks Unlimited, the donation marks one of the largest and most significant conservation easements in United States history, ensuring that this vast expanse of forests, wetlands and working farmland will remain undeveloped in perpetuity.A landscape of rare scale and qualityClarendon Farms sits in the heart of South Carolina’s coastal plain, a region known for its biodiversity, productive fisheries and deep hunting and fishing traditions. The property spans a mosaic of habitats, from mature bottomland hardwood forests and pine stands to expansive freshwater marshes and tidal creeks. Blackwater rivers such as the Santee and its tributaries flow through the land, carrying tannin-stained water that supports distinctive plant and animal communities.What makes Clarendon Farms especially remarkable is its size and continuity. In a part of the country where large tracts have been subdivided for housing, timber plantations or commercial development, 4,400 acres of intact, well-managed land is increasingly rare. The 40 miles of river and marsh frontage multiply its ecological value, creating long corridors of habitat that allow wildlife to move, feed and breed across a wide area.The decision to protect the landFor Cox Enterprises, the path to permanent protection began with a recognition that the land’s long-term value extended beyond potential real estate development, as per the report. The company had owned and managed Clarendon Farms for decades, using it for timber production, hunting leases and wildlife management. Over time, leaders within the organisation came to see the property as a legacy asset, one that could deliver lasting benefits for conservation, recreation and local communities if kept intact. The chosen approach was a conservation easement, a legal agreement in which the owner of the property voluntarily relinquishes certain rights of development but retains ownership of the land.In this case, Cox relinquished rights to subdivide or build on the property in the future. The easement is monitored by qualified conservation organisations that are responsible for managing the land and ensuring that the easement conditions are met by current and future owners of the property. By giving up development rights valued at hundreds of millions of dollars, Cox made a financial sacrifice in the traditional sense. Yet the company frames the decision as an investment in natural capital, one that yields returns in the form of clean water, wildlife habitat, carbon storage and public goodwill.What the easement coversThe conservation easement on Clarendon Farms is comprehensive in scope. It restricts residential, commercial and industrial development across the nearly 4,400 acres, preserving the land’s open, forested and wetland character. Timber harvesting and other traditional land uses can continue under sustainable management plans, but they must be carried out in ways that protect water quality, wildlife habitat and the overall ecological integrity of the property. A major focus of the easement is the protection of aquatic resources. The 40 miles of river and marsh frontage include critical spawning and nursery areas for fish such as striped bass, catfish and shad, as well as foraging grounds for wading birds, waterfowl and otters. The easement also helps to maintain natural water flows, sediment transport and nutrient cycling that help sustain the health of the entire watershed by keeping these shorelines free from docks, bulkheads and dense development. The agreement also protects cultural and historical resources on the land, including sites associated with indigenous peoples and earlier periods of European American settlement. These features add another layer of significance to a property already remarkable for its natural values.Why this matters for wildlifeFor wildlife, the permanent protection of Clarendon Farms is transformative. The South Carolina low country is a key part of the Atlantic Flyway, a migratory route used by millions of birds each year. Waterfowl such as wood ducks, teal and geese rely on the region’s flooded fields, marshes and bottomland forests for food and shelter during migration and winter. By keeping large blocks of habitat intact and well managed, the easement helps ensure that these species have places to rest and refuel as they travel thousands of miles.The property is also important for game species such as white-tailed deer and wild turkey, which thrive in the mix of mature forest, early successional habitat and agricultural openings found on Clarendon Farms. For fish, the protected river and marsh frontage provides critical connectivity between upstream spawning areas and downstream estuaries supporting life cycles that span the entire river system. In an era of accelerating habitat loss and climate change, large, connected landscapes like this are increasingly seen as refuges where wildlife can persist and adapt. The easement effectively locks in that function for generations to come.Benefits for water and peopleThe ecological benefits of protecting Clarendon Farms extend well beyond the property’s borders. Forests and wetlands serve as natural filters, trapping sediments and nutrients that would otherwise enter rivers and eventually flow into coastal estuaries. This keeps the water clear and clean, which supports fisheries, shellfish beds and recreational activities like fishing and boating. The land also helps to reduce flooding. In times of heavy rainfall, bottomland forests and marshes absorb and slowly release water, lowering peak flows downstream and reducing flood risks for nearby communities. As climate change increases the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, this buffering capacity becomes ever more valuable.For people, the protected land offers opportunities for hunting, fishing, birdwatching and nature study, though public access may be limited depending on the terms of the easement and the policies of the landowner and managing organisations. Even without broad public entry, the existence of a large, undivided tract contributes to the character of the region and supports local economies tied to outdoor recreation and natural resource-based industries.A model for large-scale conservationThe Clarendon Farms easement is being hailed as one of the most significant private land conservation actions in recent US history. Its scale, ecological quality and permanent nature set a high bar for what is possible when landowners, conservation groups and public agencies align around a shared vision. For other major landowners, particularly corporations with large real estate holdings, the donation provides an appealing model. It demonstrates that land protection can be compatible with good business sense, reputation for the brand, and long-term value creation. It also demonstrates that conservation does not necessarily imply public acquisition or government ownership. Private lands can stay in private hands and still provide public benefits through carefully crafted easements. Conservation organizations talk of the Clarendon Farms deal as proof that breakthroughs are still possible, even in areas where development pressure is high, and land prices are steep. The trick is finding partners who appreciate the inherent and practical value of keeping large landscapes whole.” Looking ahead With the easement in place, the work turns to stewardship. It will take continued attention and resources to monitor the property to ensure the terms of the easement are being met, to manage forests and wetlands for wildlife and water quality, and to adjust to evolving conditions, such as sea level rise and species distribution changes. For Cox Enterprises, the donation closes one chapter and opens another. The company no longer holds the option to develop Clarendon Farms, but it gains a lasting role in the story of one of the Southeast’s most important conservation landscapes. For wildlife, water and the people who depend on them, the protection of nearly 4,400 acres and 40 miles of river and marsh frontage is a promise that this special place will endure, not just for the next few decades, but forever.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
